title: Editable Scene Simulation for Autonomous Driving via Collaborative LLM-Agents

output_modality.value: multi-camera photo-realistic 3D scene videos rendered with a neural radiance field plus Blender-rendered inserted assets

control_signal.value: natural language commands: add or delete vehicles, choose assets, set vehicle motion, adjust viewpoint (for example moving the view 5 m ahead)

control_mechanism.value: GPT-4 agents (project manager plus tech agents) turn commands into structured JSON configurations that drive role functions: inpainting for deletion, asset bank, motion generation, view adjustment

base_model.value: McNeRF multi-camera NeRF (F2NeRF-based with alignment and exposure), McLight HDR lighting estimation, Blender foreground rendering, latent-diffusion per-frame inpainting, GPT-4 as the LLM

datasets.value: Waymo Open Dataset (front, left front, right front cameras, 40 frames per scene at 10Hz); 449 HDRIs and HoliCity for lighting

metrics.value: PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and inference time for background rendering; peak angular error and relative intensity error for lighting; command execution success rate; motion user study

controllability_evidence.value: Command execution success rates over 5 instruction categories (15 commands, 3 trials each); motion-from-text user study: ChatSim 0.988 straight, 0.940 left turn, 0.976 right turn, 0.952 speed, 1.000 within-road, versus GPT2Code and GPT2Motion.

closed_loop.value: no; scripted editing and rendering of recorded scenes, no driving policy in the loop

stated_limitations.value: Future work only: plans to add more background editing such as weather changes.

notes: Not a learned generative world model: NeRF rendering plus LLM-agent editing of a reconstructed scene. Included as a language-controlled sensor-level scene simulator. Packet shows only the first row/columns of Table 2 success rates, so no summary success number was copied.
